clean_body: Mary, Peggy, Deb, Sharice, Claire Mary, Peggy, Deb, Sharice, Claire | ~~ | | Peter, Something is happening in 18 days that has never happened in American history: Three Indigenous women are on the ballot for top statewide offices in the same year. And two more are fighting for the House seats a Democratic majority runs through. Mary Peltola , a Yup'ik leader and the first Alaska Native ever elected to Congress, leads Alaska's Senate race — the one forecasters call the "majority maker" — in a state Trump won by 13. Peggy Flanagan , a citizen of the White Earth Nation, is dead-tied at 42–42 for the seat that would make her the first Native American woman EVER in the U.S. Senate. Deb Haaland , a citizen of Laguna Pueblo and the first Native American Cabinet secretary, is defending a six-point lead to become the first Native American woman ever elected governor. Sharice Davids , a citizen of the Ho-Chunk Nation and one of the first two Native American women ever elected to Congress, is defending the seat where she made history in 2018. Claire Valdez, a citizen of the Ysleta del Sur Pueblo Nation and a union organizer, is ready to grow Indigenous representation in New York. All five are tied or ahead. But leading isn't winning, and these final 18 days are the expensive part — the ads, the doors, the mail that decide every race inside single digits. | | | Oregon didn't just adopt vote-by-mail. We INVENTED it. **So when President Trump signs an executive order restricting mail-in ballots, understand what that means: ** No state has more on the line than Oregon. This order isn't aimed at some abstract "voting system." **It targets how every single Oregonian votes.** Here's what Trump’s USPS order does. It orders the Postal Service to deliver ballots only to voters on a federal list — a list built by THIS administration. Their postmaster already said the quiet part out loud: states that don't hand over their voter data likely won't have mail ballots delivered at all. Now here's what I know. **I'm Oregon's chief elections officer. We have taken this administration to court — over their demand for your voter data, and over their first election order. We won.** _**They still are not stopping. **_ **The Constitution hasn't changed**. States run elections. Not presidents. Not postmasters. And this November, Oregon will run the same safe, fair, accurate vote-by-mail election we've run for 25 years — and I will use every power of this office to make sure of it. **[But fighting them in court is only one way to defend our elections. We must have the resources to communicate about what’s at stake — every lawsuit, every rule change, every attempt to rewrite how Oregon votes. That’s why I’m using my campaign to help travel around the state and talk directly to voters too. Peter, Last year, on live TV, Mike Lawler promised that he would not cut Medicaid. **Then he was the deciding vote on Trump’s One Big Ugly Bill that kicked nearly half a million New Yorkers off their healthcare.** But this year, he’s been campaigning on the exact opposite. He’s claiming that there have been NO Medicaid cuts at all. Meanwhile, hundreds of thousands of New Yorkers have already lost care. Mike Lawler is the worst kind of politician: self-serving and corrupt. No amount of spin can change that simple fact. Every American should have the right to access affordable healthcare. **Growing up, my dad worked as a construction worker, where his ability to earn a living depended upon his ability to stay healthy, but he could not always afford health insurance.** When it comes to ensuring working Americans like my dad can live with dignity, we need to have a strong floor and no ceiling. That means protecting and strengthening Social Security, Medicare, and Medicaid. These are non-negotiable programs we must protect. It also means lowering the cost of healthcare by taking on Big Pharma and insurance companies, and leading the charge for a public option to bring down premiums. I will fight for all of that and more when I get to Congress—because my mission is to make life easier for you. But first, we need to take on Lawler and flip this district. **FRIDAY, OCTOBER 16, 2026**
He was eleven. For five months, we had fed the chickens, cleaned their space, cuddled them, and laughed at their antics. We had raised them for food. The time came, and my son knew the task was his. We had studied _shechitah_ ; the rules were in place.
For three hours, he prayed and cried. Then he carried out the task.
He has prayed every time since. The tears belonged to that first experience alone.
There is a difference between accepting the weight of a responsibility and making an exception to escape it. The test of a principle is not whether it costs us, but whether we remain faithful to its purpose when it does.
When an exception is made, we must ask: does it honor the principle, or merely excuse us from it?
**Pause.**
**Breathe.**
**Look Deeper.**
**Refuel.**
**Welcome to Sweet Ground.**

name: Elizabeth Warren
subject: I need to be blunt about this war
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Warren for Senate
body:
We need a Congress willing to take a stand against this forever war

| | | [ ](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/216?t=3&akid=3055%2E4032634%2ERjWO8Y)
---
Forever wars don’t just happen. They’re enabled. By a president who starts a war, profits off of it, and refuses to end it. By lawmakers who could hold him accountable but choose to look away. And by a system where those who decide to go to war don’t ultimately pay the price. Trump’s war in Iran has dragged on for more than six months. Thousands of people have been killed. Families have spent months fearing for their loved ones. And the consequences of this unnecessary war will be felt for years, even generations. The bleak truth is that wars cost money — and those funds come from American pockets. Last month, the Pentagon told lawmakers the war has cost $45.1 billion. That's billions of taxpayer dollars spent on a war that keeps driving up costs for families already struggling to get by. CNN reports that the war has cost about $2,000 per American household so far, with another $50 added every week it continues. Gas is averaging $4.34 a gallon. Diesel, which powers the trucks, tractors, and trains that keep our economy moving, is near record highs. Homes using heating oil are expected to pay 21% more for the fuel than last winter. And while working families are stretching every paycheck, Trump’s largest oil and gas holdings gained an estimated $1.5 million to $4.4 million in the war’s first six months. Families are paying more. Trump’s oil and gas interests are making more. And the war just keeps going. This cannot continue. Congress has both the power and the responsibility to stop this war. Under the War Powers Act, lawmakers can force a vote on ending unauthorized U.S. military involvement in Iran. But Republicans have allowed Trump to prolong this conflict instead of using their power to bring it to an end. I know many of you are angry about what this administration is doing. I am, too. I grieve for everyone killed in this conflict, and I think about the families at home trying to understand why their loved ones are being sent into a war with no clear end in sight. They deserve answers. They deserve accountability. And they deserve a Congress willing to use every tool it has to end this war. We can end this war. And I’ll keep fighting to make sure we do. Thanks for being a part of this, Elizabeth

**FROM EVIDENCE TO ACTION**
* **THE FACTS:** What does Philadelphia's academic performance reveal, and what can Mississippi's remarkable progress teach us?
* **THE STANDARD:** What should every child know, understand, and be capable of doing before entering adulthood?
* **THE SOLUTIONS:** What actually builds success, and what roles must parents, educators, pastors, and community leaders play?
* **THE REALITIES:** An honest conversation about the streets, the system, and the obstacles facing Philadelphia's young people.
* **THE ACTION:** _Philadelphia, What Now?_ An opportunity for attendees to help identify practical next steps for our homes, schools, and communities.

This is where you become part of the conversation.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a2398720-12d9-450e-b672-bc8d5e6c4677?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
We're not bringing people together simply to listen to experts. We're bringing people together to learn from one another, challenge assumptions, raise expectations, and identify what we can begin doing in our own homes, schools, and communities.
**[Because the future of our children is too important to leave to government.](https://substack.com/redirect/a2398720-12d9-450e-b672-bc8d5e6c4677?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Join us.
**Saturday, October 24, 2026 | 9 a.m. -2 p.m.**
📍 Braid Mill, 441 E. High Street, Germantown, Philadelphia
Doors open at 8:30 a.m. Caribbean fusion brunch included.
Tickets start at $35. **Pastors, teachers, and Germantown residents attend FREE.** Registration is required, and seating is limited.
[RESERVE YOUR SEAT TODAY](https://substack.com/redirect/a2398720-12d9-450e-b672-bc8d5e6c4677?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
**If Mississippi can do it, surely Philadelphia can too.**
Let's get to work!

| | **_Meet Russell:_** Born and raised in Surfside Beach, SC, Congressman Russell Fry is the proud and homegrown Representative for South Carolina’s 7th Congressional District. Growing up in a cinder block home with no heating or air conditioning, Russell learned at an early age that hard work and perseverance pave the only true path to the American Dream. He watched his parents work day in and day out to make ends meet. And the values they instilled in him during his upbringing led Russell to self-fund both his undergraduate education at the University of South Carolina, and later his law studies at the Charleston School of Law. At Charleston, Russell served as the President of the Student Bar Association and even helped the school achieve its American Bar Association accreditation. He went on to practice law in the Grand Strand area for over a decade before entering the political arena to serve in the South Carolina House of Representatives for State House District 106 (Horry County). During his seven-year tenure in the SC House, Russell fought to safeguard Constitutional liberties, lower taxes, and put the best interests of South Carolina families above all else. He climbed the ranks to become Chief Majority Whip, and also chaired the House Opioid Prevention Study Committee. Under Russell’s leadership, 18 policy initiatives to combat the opioid crisis were signed into law. Since the first day he stepped foot in Washington, Russell has strived to shake up the corrupt status quo and deliver real change for the American people. He believes adamantly that so long as the American people stand united, we can keep the American Dream alive for every citizen of our great nation.
